title: sequence and string dynamic programming
concepts: Sequence DP often defines a state over a prefix, ending position, or pair of positions, with transitions that match, skip, extend, or restart a candidate subsequence.
A subsequence preserves relative order but may skip elements; a substring is contiguous, so their recurrences and boundary rules differ.
Longest common subsequence uses two prefix indices and considers matching characters or skipping one side; reconstruction follows stored or recomputed choices.
Longest increasing subsequence has an O(n²) endpoint DP and an O(n log n) tails optimization that stores minimum tail values rather than the full subsequence history.
String edit distance uses prefix pairs and models insert, delete, and replace operations; initialization handles converting a prefix to or from an empty string.
Palindromic substring problems depend on contiguous ranges and interval expansion, while palindromic subsequence problems allow skipped characters and use interval states.
Space compression for two-string DP can retain adjacent rows, but direction and reconstruction requirements may prevent discarding earlier state.
Common errors include off-by-one prefix indexing, confusing substring with subsequence, and omitting empty-prefix base cases.
